header.title: Libellus Adversus Fulgentium Donatistam: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Augustine, Saint
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's stoa0040.stoa070a.opp-lat1, from Open Greek and Latin's CSEL (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. The whole work is translated. It was chosen because no English translation of it could be found.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation of the whole work, checked against the original by a second AI only in samples. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0040.stoa070a.opp-l: 1.1: 'tam obice forte prima fronte' is awkward and probably corrupt; rendered as 'as an obstacle strong perhaps at first sight'. 'moriturae muscae' (Eccl. 10:1) rendered 'dying flies'. 'ut hactenus uictores' translated literally ('so that thus far'); the sense is uncertain. 2.3: the trailing '-.' is a scanning artefact. 3.1: the clause 'alterum, quod semel potandorum meatibus...' is syntactically obscure; translated loosely. 4.2: 'ego in nobis' read as 'ego in uobis' ('I in you'); 'plectatur' ('is punished') makes poor sense, and a reading such as 'plicatur/implicatur' ('is entangled') may be intended. 5.2: the parenthesised words in Zechariah are an editorial supplement; 'in partem ducamus' rendered 'draw off ... into a faction'.

‘traditores’ rendered ‘traditors’ (those who handed over scriptures in persecution). In 10.1 ‘aperta confectio’ is obscure; ‘confectio’ taken as the preparation of the sacrament (chrism). Habakkuk 3:15 and Hosea 6:8–9 are run together as one quotation. ‘deleticia’ read as ‘delicias/deliciae’; sense uncertain. In 6.2 ‘sed ut legitime uiuat in ipsa uiuat’ is awkward; rendered by sense. ‘male bene’ taken as ‘male (aut) bene’.

13.1: the clause 'vel in abruptum cenosi gurgitis lacum ... Charybdis vidit et exterminii oleum flammis edacibus animavit' is syntactically broken and probably corrupt (the accusative 'pestes' after 'ubi' is also irregular); the rendering is tentative. 14.1 'confectio suavitatis': the Vulgate of Eccl. 10:1 has 'suavitatem unguenti'; here rendered literally. 16.2: in the honey simile the text is compressed; '[into the wormwood]' is supplied for sense. 18.1 'per colles tortuosos' is uncertain in sense.

20.2: the subject of 'Omnes' is unstated; the 'pirate's mark' that follows suggests pirates are meant, presumably carried over from a lost or compressed context. 'exsufflo/exsufflant' refers to the rite of exorcising by breathing out on a person. 22.5: 'mens' read as 'meus' (scanning error). 23.10: 'peccantes colaphizantes' appears corrupt; translated as 'when you sin, you endure being beaten' (cf. 1 Pet 2:20 'peccantes et colaphizati'). 26.2: 'cognito ululatu suo' is obscure; rendered literally.
'traditio uestra' plays on 'traditio' (tradition) and the Donatist charge of 'traditio' (handing over the scriptures); the pun cannot be kept in English.

nodes.text: The little book which your reverence, brother Fulgentius, sent me I have received without scorn; whether you composed it yourself or sought it from elsewhere, I do not now much concern myself. For this too is a duty of our religion: not to fix our attention on persons, but to seek the truth in all things, to recognize it when found, and to keep it once acknowledged. For so the apostle Paul says: Test all things, hold fast what is good; abstain from every evil appearance. I will therefore state briefly what you have spread out rather ingeniously in writing. You said that there is one baptism, which the Samaritan, that is, the heretic, has not deserved to have; that the one enclosed garden, which is the church, has a sealed fountain, which no outsider touches; that there is one oil, which is the most holy chrism, which dying flies corrupt and which sinners will by no means give. Against these things I must prepare a reply with the Lord's help, and take it from nowhere else than from the divine reading. Let us then now take up the beginning of the word; or rather, let us hold to the Word himself, the beginning of the laws, the Lord, the leader and prince of the heavenly host; let us wage war and, with the sacred trumpet in his hand, assail the mighty walls of the wicked city of Jericho, that is, let us encircle the height of worldly wisdom with the Lord's testaments, let us make it resound with the voices of truth and freedom, let us compel our adversaries to flee for refuge into the house of Rahab, that is, of the church, which receives his messengers, because of the destruction of the world, and let us condemn the obstinate with anathema, so that thus far we may be victors. These things, then, you have taken from the law against the law, from God's testament against God's testament, from the fountain of truth against the fountain of truth, as an obstacle strong perhaps at first sight, as if truth could be defeated by itself, or the glory of light be darkened by its own light.

The Donatist said: Our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, teacher and guardian of the one baptism, lest error of mind should lead thirsting souls to dry cisterns, proclaiming that perennial draughts are in himself, testified thus in his gospel, saying: Let him who thirsts come and drink, he who believes in me, as Isaiah says.
The Catholic replied: It does not have 'as Isaiah says', but 'as the scripture says'. But I will disregard such things as hindrances, and not shut out the reader's profit with a long discourse.

The Donatist said: He who believes in me, as Isaiah said, rivers of living water will flow from his belly. And lest it be said that one could drink anywhere and everywhere, he himself distinguished the merits of waters, when he condemned the origin of Samaria's apostasy at its own fountain: He who drinks, he says, of this water will thirst again; he who drinks of the water which I shall give will not thirst for ever, but there will be in him a fountain of water springing up into eternal life.

The Catholic replied: You have certainly set these things down in order to show us Catholics to be, as it were, Samaritans and without baptism. Now then, begin to look upon the Donatists as Samaritans. The doctrine of the Samaritans, as the book of Kings teaches, was this: they feared God and at the same time worshipped images; they kept the divine law and by no means abandoned the errors of their fathers; they had the sign of circumcision and did not keep the fellowship of the Israelites. You too do this. You fear God and likewise worship a clay image, Donatus — for he too was fashioned from earth —; you keep the divine law and do not abandon the error of your parents; you have the sacrament of baptism and do not wish to have fellowship with the Catholics. See, you resemble them in all things. As, then, the circumcision of the Samaritans could not be given a second time, so now the baptism of the Donatists ought not to be repeated, as the Lord Christ teaches: He who has once been washed has no need to be washed again. For the circumcision of the Samaritans signifies the baptism of the Donatists, as the apostle says: You have been circumcised with a circumcision not made by hand, in the stripping off of the body of the flesh, but in the circumcision of Christ, buried with him in baptism. But when the Lord says: He who drinks of this water will thirst again, he spoke not of baptism but of the earthly element. For if he had wished to point to baptism here, he would in no way have asked the Samaritan woman for a drink. Finally, that well was called not Samaria's but Jacob's; and Jacob was certainly not a heretic, but beloved of God, ever dear, and he himself drank from it, and his sons and his flocks.

The Donatist said: The spirit of the church, then, never allows to be joined to it what has deserved to be defamed by the divine mouth, as the proclamation of the law forewarns: two and two, one against one; and the Lord in the gospel: Then, he says, two will be in the field; one will be taken and one will be left. Two women grinding at the mill; one will be taken and one will be left. You see, then, that there are two kinds of baptism and two rewards of merit: while the one is burned up by the heat of a deadly disposition, and a drinking thirst parches away its perennial draughts, the other, once it has passed through the channels of those who are to drink, satisfies thirst with the perpetuity of life. Certainly he shows perpetual dryness in dug-out pools, and while he closed off to them the merit of life, he opened the approach of death, as Jeremiah says: This people commits two evils. They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and have dug for themselves worn-out cisterns which cannot hold water; and again: Let all who forsake you be confounded; let those who depart from you be written in the book of death; because they have forsaken you, let those who depart from you, the fountain of life, be confounded.

The Catholic replied: You [set] one against one; I assert many baptisms against the one. For the pagan baptizes, and the Jew baptizes, and the Sadducee baptizes, and many outside the rule of the given law do not cease to baptize. But that one is the one which is true, that is true which is Christ's, that is Christ's which is of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. This is true, this is saving; nothing is to be compared with it. Whoever does not receive this has himself both closed off for himself the merit of life and opened the approach of death.

The Donatist said: But if, as you assert, one faith subsists in both, why did he distinguish by a just separation between faithful water and faithless, as the Lord testifies through Isaiah: Who has announced to you that the fire burns? Who has announced to you that eternal place? He who walks in righteousness, proclaiming the right way, hating crime and injustice, and keeping his hands from gifts, and stopping his ear so as not to hear a judgment of blood, and shutting his eyes so that they do not see iniquity, he will dwell in lofty hope; strong bread will be given him, and his water will be faithful. And separating the faithless [water] from its faith, he set it down thus, as Jeremiah testifies: Why do those who wrong me prevail? My wound has become solid: how shall I heal? It has become to me like lying water that has no faithfulness.

The Catholic replied: All heretics, though they disagree among themselves in their own disputation, yet agree on the solemn formula in the handing on of baptism, just as one circumcision, but with differing faith, subsisted among the Jews and the Samaritans of old. It is necessary, then, that as then, so now it should be done for converts, that what is punished by disputation alone should again be undone by disputation alone, so that they may hear from the Lord: You are already clean because of the word which I have spoken to you; abide in me, and I in you. For all these things happened to them in figure, but they were written for our correction, upon whom the ends of the ages have come.

The Donatist said: Ezekiel also speaks thus: And they saw that there are many who have turned away the water of the ancient pool, and they did not look to him who made it from the beginning, and they did not see him who founded it. Unheard-of madness of the faithless, to be unwilling to believe the divine voices, and unwilling to preserve the simple teaching of the apostle from the jaws of their own error!

The Catholic replied: Far be it, far be it from us to draw off the water of the ancient pool into a faction, as you do, or not to believe the divine utterances. What we read we believe, and what we believe we preach. Hear what our origin is and where its water has been spread abroad. In Zechariah you have it thus: Living waters will go out from Jerusalem; half of them to the eastern sea and half of them to the furthest sea — that is, from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth —; in summer and in winter they will be — that is, they will be at all times —; and the Lord will be king over all the earth, that is, Christ will rule over all the earth, not Donatus. This is the possession, this the inheritance of Christ, which is tilled by the saints and watered by a perennial fountain, concerning which it was said to him: I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession. Whoever is in it is enrolled as an heir; whoever is not in it is already condemned and destined for death, as the scripture says: Whoever goes out of the doors of your house will be guilty against himself.

The Donatist said: Hence God proclaims that there is a single baptism of his own, hence the apostle confirms that he spoke of one to all, God proving it through Solomon: An enclosed garden, my sister, my bride, a sealed fountain, a well of living water, a paradise with the fruit of apples.

The Catholic replied: Remember the law and pay careful attention, and see that from this paradise, from this enclosed garden, from this sealed fountain, the wave of salvation runs down even outside, which goes against the Assyrians, that is, against you Donatists. For from the Assyrians are born those Samaritans who have been compared to you. It is, says the scripture, the river that goes against the Assyrians, against the nation hostile to the people of God. It does not go for them, but against [them]. For to some it is the odour of death unto death, but to others the odour of life unto life. For just as whoever eats and drinks the blood of the Lord unworthily eats and drinks judgement on himself, so also whoever receives baptism unworthily receives judgement on himself, not salvation. For Judas the traitor too received the good body, and Simon Magus the good baptism of Christ, but because they did not use the good well, being evil they were destroyed by using it badly. Baptism is good, the blood and body of Christ are good, the law too is good, but if one uses them lawfully. Nor is it not divine because it is also outside, nor will it be thought alien because it is held by aliens, nor will it be condemned by us justly because it is handled unjustly by the wicked. The water of paradise is the water of the Trinity. Where we recognise this, we do not deny that it is of paradise; where we do not discern this, we do not call it of paradise at all. Whatever has arisen outside is in no way to be called of paradise: for instance the Manichee, because he was never in paradise and did not go out from the Church as you did, is not to be thought the water of paradise, because he arose outside. This one needs to live, lest he die for ever; but to live lawfully, let him live in it [the Church], lest he eat and drink judgement.

The Donatist said: On the contrary, the apostle bears witness that he said: One God, one faith, one baptism. There is no variation in divine teaching; in all things the servant follows the Lord, in nothing does the disciple differ from the master.

The Catholic replied: Whom do you follow, whom do you imitate, whom do you judge to be the author of this outrage? Give me any of the saints after the Trinity who rebaptised, as you do. Read me not those scriptures by whose authority I am not bound, but those of the New and Old Testament, to which we are both subject. If baptism is one, why do you double the one? For you repeat nothing other than what you find true. Since, therefore, as he said, you rebuild the things you destroyed, you show yourselves to be transgressors.

The Donatist said: Or if you think the sacrament of baptism one, joined with the guilty by some mixing, hear the prophets [say] by whom it is rightly dispensed, as Solomon says: The fountain of life is in the hands of the just.

The Catholic replied: The Lord spoke well of you, who foresaw your error beforehand: You who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts, for what is lofty among men is abominable before God. If you are just and the fountain of life is in your hand, you are not a man but God. Let people flee to you, let them believe in you, let all hope of life be placed in you, let baptism itself be given in your name and let the Lord be passed over in silence. Do you want to know where to seek this fountain of life? You have it in the psalm: With you is the fountain of life, and in your light we shall see light. Have you not read: A wicked son has proud eyes, a wicked son calls himself just, but he will not wash away his own goings out? Unless you recognise that, as a man, you are guilty, unless you cry out with a truthful heart that you are a sinner, you will not be able to be justified at all, as the prophet says: Tell your iniquities, that you may be justified. And the apostle John: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.
The Donatist said: And David says: But let not the oil of the sinner fatten my head.

The Catholic replied: Then give me any one of your people whom you can prove not to be a sinner, so that your oil cannot be a sinner’s, since it is written: There is no man who does not sin. You interpret badly; read from above, so that you can grasp the sense. It says thus: The just man will correct me in mercy and rebuke me; but let not the oil of the sinner anoint my head; that is: a merciful rebuke is better than gentle flattery, as also that saying: Better are the wounds of a friend than the willing kisses of an enemy. The oil of the sinner is the blandishment of the flatterer, of whom it says elsewhere: His words are softer than oil, and they are darts. The oil of the just is the Spirit of God, as Peter says: Jesus of Nazareth, whom God anointed with the Holy Spirit. So stop calling the Holy Spirit the oil of a sinner, lest you begin to declare God a sinner.

The Donatist said: In this place is shown the evident preparation of the faithless, which, touched with hostile presumption by a criminal priest, is polluted, and whose sacrifice, like oil, is rejected by the divine voice. The criminal, it says, who sacrifices a calf to me is as one who kills a dog, and he who offers fine flour as [one who offers] swine’s blood, and he who offers incense for a memorial as a blasphemer.

The Catholic replied: It is certain that God curses and despises the burnt offerings of priest and people if a good conscience is not present. Or if you want it understood as said of priests alone, how is the preparation of criminal priests not polluted among you? You say: ‘As long as the wicked are hidden they cannot defile, because of which it is written: What is hidden is mine, what is manifest is yours.’ If, then, as long as the wicked are hidden they cannot defile, why are you not afraid to rebaptise distant nations, to whom the name of Donatus and Caecilian is unknown? Which of you ever brought the evil deeds of any people to their knowledge? And even if he had brought it and not proved it, it would do no harm at all, according to that saying: What is hidden is mine, what is manifest is yours.

The Donatist said: Further, the prophet Habakkuk reveals its waters by the Spirit: You have set your horses in the sea, it says, troubling many waters. The city of Gilead has despised me, which works foolish things, troubling the waters. And your strength is like that of a pirate.

The Catholic replied: Recognise your own weapons in yourself, as it is written: Let their sword enter into their own hearts and let their bow be broken. Your strength, Donatist, is like that of a pirate, you who rebaptise by force, fight by force in the water, kill by force in the water. Doing such things, you will be captured and killed as a pirate, unless you are converted and repent and serve as a soldier of Christ the king in the Catholic [Church].

The Donatist said: If, then, the Church glories in a single fountain, surely it is the den of the traditors that is puffed up in a multitude of waters and, confused by the drunkenness of its baptism, commits fornication with kings, as John says: Come, I will show you the condemnation of the great harlot who sits upon many waters, and all who dwell on the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication. I ask, what are the many waters but many baptisms? What is the fornicating woman but the den of the traditors, which serves, in thrall, the pleasures of kings, from whom drinking the cup of persecution she mixes it, drunk with blindness, for the peoples, and leads into madness those she has watered? Approach to her the most wise Solomon forbade: Keep yourself, he says, from alien water, and do not drink from an alien fountain, that you may live a long time, and the years of your life will be added to you. Let the fountain of your water be private to you: let no stranger share it with you. He alone, then, has no private fountain who by the power of the harlot possesses a multitude of waters. The apostle John too condemns the multitude of waters, saying: And the angel said to me: The waters which you saw, on which that fornicator sits, are peoples, crowds and nations.

The Catholic replied: As I see, wherever water is named, badly or well, you have taken it to be baptism. If in a good sense, you wanted to assign it to yourself; if in a bad sense, to me; so that what the apostle Paul said would be fulfilled in you: Knowing neither what they say nor about what they make assertions. For just as Jannes and Jambres resisted Moses, so these resist the truth. The angel says: The waters which you saw are peoples, crowds and nations. And you resist the angel who explains it and say: ‘I ask, what are the many waters but many baptisms? What is the fornicating woman but the den of the traditors?’ If you want also to learn the names of traditors, you have your own: Silvanus of Cirta handing over the sacred things to Felix the curator; you have Marianus of Aquae Tibilitanae offering three codices to Romanus the curator; you have Victor of Rusicade burning the four gospels as if they were delicacies; who dared to condemn Caecilian, innocent and absent. This is the den of thieves, this the offspring of traditors, this the fornicating woman who, abandoning Christ, has prostituted her brothels to Donatus, whose house, according to Solomon, is the retreat of death, whose ways are those of the underworld, who calls herself clean though she is full of filth, who cries that she is innocent though she is entangled in crimes, who commits shameful deeds and attributes her own acts to another, lest she first hear what she has committed. For you defame Catholics with your own deeds, so as to separate the peoples from the Lord. Accordingly, as for your exhorting, as it were, your own people to keep away from our water, and saying: Keep yourself from alien water and do not drink from an alien fountain; let the fountain of your water be private to you: let no stranger share it with you, who does not see that the prophet was commending chastity to married people, and that you have strayed far from the truth? Or if no stranger ought to share in your fountain, why do you seek strangers, why do you rebaptise Catholics?

The Donatist said: It is clear, then, that among the traditors there is a multitude of waters, where there are the various seeds of schisms, where the manifold plagues of heretics, where the detestable dregs of the filth of the Manichees, or where Charybdis has seen [men] snatched into eternal death in the steep pool of a muddy whirlpool, and has fanned the oil of destruction with devouring flames. The Catholic replied: O what proof, O what error, O what raving! 'It is clear, then, that among the traditors there is a multitude of waters, where there are the various seeds of schisms, where the manifold plagues of heretics, where the detestable dregs of the filth of the Manichees'? How do you prove that the manifold plagues of schismatics are with us? If they were with us, they would not be heretics but Catholics.

The Donatist said: Hear Solomon saying: Dying flies destroy the preparation of sweetness. The sweetness of oil, then, is inborn, and if it has been violated by a wicked touch it becomes unpleasant, the preparation polluted. And rightly has the Holy Spirit likened the traditors to unclean winged creatures, because they wickedly fall upon another's table and foul the sweetness of the oil with unclean touches.

The Catholic replied: Who violates by a wicked touch? He who preserves what he has found, or he who shamelessly destroys what has been prepared? When did we touch your oil, when did we drive away the Holy Spirit by blowing [it] out? Show that any one of us has wickedly fallen upon the oil of the Godhead, or has unlawfully violated the baptism of the Trinity as you do. The dying flies, the Donatists, fly round through the limbs of the whole body; wherever they find [them] wounded, they sting the healthy, lick the sick, and pour into their sores the worms of sins, which gnaw the conscience, which make an end of the soul, which feed putrefaction, which spare not even the dead corpses themselves. Dying flies, when they destroy the oil, perish by the oil; for you who breathe out the Holy Spirit do not live.

The Donatist said: This the most holy David properly teaches, supplying the rule of our faith: that the oil of the sinner neither brings salvation nor ought to touch anyone's head. Let not the oil of the sinner, he says, anoint my head. Therefore the person of the sinner must be sought out by careful examination, if the Lord did not speak of a sacrilegious priest, as the profane assert.

The Catholic replied: Though you are conscious of sin, do you dare to say: 'the person of the sinner must be sought out'? Hear who this person of the sinner is. The apostle said: All have sinned and lack the glory of God; and Solomon: There is no one among men who does not sin; and Job: If he found depravity in his angels, how much more in the sons of men, who have an earthly dwelling! This is the person of the sinner, that is, every man is a sinner. If you are a priest, you are a man, and if you are a man, you are a sinner. Whom do you make yourself? You have said that you alone are holy, you alone just, you alone without sin, you alone without stain. You have said that baptism is yours, the holy oil yours, the Lord's table yours, all those things yours which are divinely bestowed on the faithful. What remains, except that you wickedly and impiously declare yourself to be God? But hear what the head of pride deserved to hear: How you have fallen from heaven, Lucifer, who rose in the morning, who wounded the nations, who said in your heart: I will ascend above heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the mountain of the covenant in the sides of the north, and I will be like the Most High? Yet you shall go down to hell and into the depth of the pit. Unless, then, you repent, unless you are converted, unless you lay aside pride and ask pardon for your sins, you will hear what he too heard, because, though you are a man, you make yourself God.

The Donatist said: Likewise the Lord, through the prophet Haggai, showed by a wholesome exposition that unclean touches bring defilement, and that no polluted person can sanctify, if with unlawful presumption he tries to touch what he sees to be held holy, when he set forth the prophet as a warning for us: Ask the priests, says the Lord, saying: If a man binds holy flesh in the hem of his garment, and the hem of the garment touches any creature of bread or wine or oil, is it sanctified? And the priests answered and said: No. And the Lord said: If one defiled in soul touches any of these, will it be defiled? And the priests said: It will be defiled. And the Lord said: So too is this people and so this nation: everyone who approaches there will be defiled.

The Catholic replied: You have used this testimony against yourself, you who place the gift of God in your own choice. For if the touch of the holy does not remove the defilements of the unclean, what you perform, what you prepare, what you wash is vain. If, it says, what is holy touches a creature of bread or wine or oil, will it be sanctified? And the priests answered and said: No. Where is that in which you exalt yourselves, your boast that your holiness confers cleanness? Or if you are moved by what it says: So this people and so this nation: everyone who approaches there will be defiled, show that Haggai, who taught these things, went out from the midst of that same people, so that he himself should not be polluted among them. That touch signifies works. If, it says, a holy man touches the unclean, it will not be sanctified; if an unclean man touches the holy, it will be defiled; that is: a holy man who has been joined to this most wicked nation is more easily made wicked than this nation is changed for the better, because one runs more readily to imitating the wicked than the mind is roused to the virtues of the good; just as a little wormwood thrown into much honey quickly draws [it] to bitterness, but even if double [the amount] of honey is thrown into [the wormwood], its sweetness cannot prevail. We must go out from the midst of the wicked in mind, not in flesh, in works, not in bodies. Do not, says the apostle, take part in the unfruitful works of darkness. He says 'works', not 'altars'. For it is written in Isaiah: Those who say: Go away from me, do not come near me, for you are unclean, these shall be smoke in my anger, a fire burning all day. If the words of men do not frighten you, at least let the anger of God threatening convert you.

The Donatist said: Never has a robber brought his plunder into the light; always the workers of the night have shuddered more fiercely at the light, welcome to all good men; only the traditor is not broken even by the threats of God, and wickedly glories in another's garment. Against him the Lord cries out through Zephaniah and is not heard: It shall be, he says, on the day of the Lord's sacrifice, and I will take vengeance on the princes and on all who are clothed in alien garments.

The Catholic replied: I do not fear your accusations, because my conscience is protected. The one you say handed over [the Scriptures], show the name and place of that traditor. You will never be able to show it, just as you were not able before. But even if you bring someone forward, he cannot harm me, as the Lord says: The soul of the father is mine, the soul of the son is mine. The soul that has sinned, it alone shall die. Yet I do not rejoice in another's garment, I who always exult in the Catholic faith. That is the [garment] I have, with which on the day of redemption the merciful and kind Father clothed me in beauty: Bring, he says, that first robe and put it on him, for this my son was dead and has come back to life, he was lost and has been found; that very [robe], surely, of which the apostle Paul said: As many of you as have been baptised in Christ have put on Christ. This I have, in this I rejoice, in this I shall always appear more glorious. This is what you have either taken away like robbers or, wretched men, defile.

The Donatist said: For inasmuch as wickedness desires to attach devious errors to the goods of others, and tries to cover the false Catholic [Church] with clouds of lies, it walks over winding hills; the Lord met it as an opponent through Jeremiah: Do not trust in false words, he says, for they will not profit you at all, saying: The temple of the Lord is the temple of God. And the Lord in Deuteronomy: Take heed to yourself that you do not offer burnt offerings in every place that you see, but in the place which the Lord your God shall choose in your tribe; in this you shall offer burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I command you today.

The Catholic replied: You have cited a testimony excellently, and very fitting for your salvation: Take heed to yourself that you do not offer burnt offerings in every place that you see, but in the place which the Lord your God shall choose in your tribe; in this you shall offer burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that he shall command you. Hear, then, which is the chosen place and which the tribe of the Lord that is proclaimed. In the hundred and thirty-first psalm you have: For the Lord has chosen Zion, he has chosen it for a dwelling for himself; this is my rest for ever and ever, here I will dwell, for I have chosen it. Likewise in the hundred and twenty-first psalm: Our feet were standing in your courts, Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which is built as a city. For there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord, the testimony of Israel. This is the chosen place, this the sanctified mountain, this the city set on a mountain so that it cannot be hidden, this the Catholic root, this the fruitful vine spread far and wide, which in Ecclesiasticus cries out and says: In Zion I was established and in Jerusalem is my power. For so it behoved Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead on the third day, and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name throughout all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. You would rightly rebuke me if you remained in this inheritance. But since you do not remain in this inheritance of God the Father, do not serve as a soldier in this tribe of Christ the king, why do you, a deserter, reprove the soldier, why do you, the guilty one, chide the innocent? And I say to you: Take heed to yourself that you do not offer in every place, that is, in every heresy, and say: 'God is both here and there'; but in the place which the Lord your God shall choose in your tribe, that is, in his tribe, there you shall offer your burnt offerings and there you shall do all that has been commanded you. Do this, and you will live.

The Donatist said: So that cannot be called baptism which the crowd of waters has scattered, which malice has separated from the fountain of the Church, which a barren wave has dried up, which has seen neither an angel nor found a prophet who could heal it, just as in the fourth book of Kingdoms the most holy Elisha healed deadly waters, driving out death, and by a fertilising word let them flow into abundant offspring: And the men of the city said to Elisha: Behold, the situation of the city is good, as you yourself, lord, see, but the waters here are bad and barren. And Elisha said: Bring me a new earthen vessel and put salt in it. And they brought it, and he went to the outflow of the waters and threw in the salt and said: Thus says the Lord: I have healed these waters, and there shall be no more death in them nor barrenness. And the waters were healed to this day.

The Catholic answered: Thanks be to God the Father, who faithfully fulfilled in us what he showed would come. Thanks, I say, to God the Father, who sent to us, into our Jericho, that is, into this world, not angels only, not prophets, as before, but his own Son, namely the Lord of angels and the prince of prophets, to heal the barrenness of the waters, that is, the unfruitfulness of the nations, driving out death. He took an earthen vessel, that is, the body of human frailty; he put in salt, that is, he filled it with divine wisdom; he threw it into the water, that is, he went down into the Jordan; he healed the waters by his descent, that is, he redeemed the nations by his coming; and by a fertilising word he gathered the Church out of the nations and spread it far and wide into abundant offspring. Whoever does not see that this has been fulfilled in us is blind; whoever does not believe it is mad. Look at the abundant offspring: say where this Church is not; say where yours is found except in a corner of Africa, badly gathered like a useless cutting. Where it was cut off from this [Church], there it has stayed; it could not spread further, because, cut off from the root, it at once withered.

The Donatist said: One city of the Saviour received the substance of the water; one widow together with her children received also the gift of oil, nor did the prophet entrust the divine benefit to anyone indiscriminately, but only to her whom he knew to have one vessel of oil, as the truth of Kingdoms proves: And a woman, one of the wives of the prophets, cried out after Elisha, saying: Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared God. And behold, those to whom I owe [money] have come to take my two sons as slaves. And Elisha said: What shall I do? Tell me what you have in your house. And she said: Your handmaid has nothing in the house except one vessel of oil. And Elisha said: Go, ask for vessels from outside, from all who dwell near you, many vessels, and you shall go in and shut the door upon yourself and your sons, and you shall fill the vessels with oil and pay the debt. For Elisha worked through the outlines of true baptism. Indeed, because I do not approve yours, therefore I exorcise your faithful by breathing on them.

The Catholic answered: But all [pirates] do what you too do. All of them breathe out on the faithful, while claiming for themselves the single sacrament of baptism. When you find such a one, will you not seize him, not hold him, not bind him with this chain, but, recognising the pirate's mark, will you let him go away safe, so that he may carry on his trade with you?
Fulgentius said: Far be it from me to let him go away, since God said: Compel all to come in, that my house may be filled. He who said 'all' excepted no one.
Augustine answered: What then will you do?
Fulgentius said: I shall teach him that my Church is the most certain.
Augustine answered: In what way? Will you show that Christ, who received all nations from the Father, has remained only in an African fragment?
Fulgentius said: I shall say that it consists in few.
Augustine answered: What if he too has few? For all have few in comparison with the Catholic [Church].
Fulgentius said: I shall show that the true one is that which suffers persecution, not that which inflicts it.
Augustine answered: What if his [church] too has inflicted no persecution at all?
Fulgentius said: I shall suggest, following the apostle, that my Church alone has no wrinkles or spots.

Augustine answered: It will at once be proved to have them. For it is written: No one is clean from filth, not even if his life on earth has been of one day. But why say more? By whatever skill you seize and hold him, how do you receive the one who perhaps re-dipped your faithful, who extinguished the Holy Spirit in the heart of a believer?
Fulgentius said: I restrain him, I breathe out on him, and I baptise him with true water for the remission of sins.

Augustine answered: How do you forgive his sins, when it is written that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit cannot be forgiven for ever? But let us leave this; let us look at another thing. Say also to the Maximianist, your rival, what you said to me: 'How can another have it, if it has been granted to me alone? Or if you claim it was handed over to your right, why do you approve another's?' And this Maximianist will answer: 'How can another not have it, when you have proved that it has been granted to me as to you? For you received my Christians and clergy, baptised or ordained outside your Church, entire, without any change of baptism or rank!' This, when it was put to you in the proceedings of Marcellinus, you were in no way able to refute.
Augustine answered again: If you are just, why is your judgement inconsistent? Why do you receive the Maximianist and exorcise my faithful by breathing on them?
Fulgentius said: Because he was mine.
Augustine answered: And you were mine. Why do you persist in being merciful to your schismatic, and pitiless and implacable to the Catholic?
Fulgentius said: You sinned more, and therefore it is punished differently in you.

Augustine answered: What then? Do you set up baptism as a punishment, and is what is promised for salvation given by you as a penalty? If in baptism you do not forgive offences but chastise sins, if in the water you do not set free but scourge, you plainly show that you are a pirate. But still, how did I sin more, what did I do?
Fulgentius said: You handed over the books and sacrificed to idols.
Augustine answered: Prove it. I did not do it; you are pinning your own deeds on me.
Fulgentius said: Your father did it.
Augustine answered: I know no father except God. For it is written: Do not call anyone on earth your father; for you have one Father, the heavenly one.
Fulgentius said: By your father I mean Caecilian. He handed over, he offered incense, he committed every evil.

Augustine answered: Read out who accused him, who convicted him, who condemned him in his presence. Suppose he did what he did not do: shall I, the son, be condemned for the father, when it is written: The soul of the father is mine and the soul of the son is mine. The soul that has sinned, it alone shall die?
Fulgentius said: You, his son, did not indeed hand over, but you inflicted persecution on us.

Augustine answered: I certainly did not, but I believe that my people may have done so. I ask the reason why. What if you deserved it? For it is not a sin to persecute the wicked. Indeed we read that the wicked persecuted both the saints and the Lord, the Holy of holies. For the demons, unable to bear the Lord's persecution, cried out: What have we to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come to destroy us? And Paul punished Elymas the magician with blindness and handed a blasphemous man over to Satan, and Peter killed the liars Ananias and Sapphira his wife, and persecuted Simon the magician until he destroyed him by death. And David too, in the person of Christ, cries out and says: I will pursue my enemies and overtake them, and I will not turn back until they fail. I will afflict them and they will not be able to stand. Not everyone, therefore, who has suffered persecution is at once to be thought just, but he who has suffered for righteousness' sake is truly blessed, as Peter says: For what glory is it if, when you sin, you endure being beaten? But if, doing good, you suffer and endure patiently, this is grace with God.
Fulgentius said: The saints you mention did not obtain edicts from secular judges, as your people did.

Augustine answered: Either it is lawful or it is not. If it is lawful, it is not fitting to grumble about what is lawful; if it is not lawful, amend your crime while you may. For you persecuted your schismatics the Maximianists, as the records declare, with the authority of secular judges, the support of various orders, and the enforcement of various soldiers, appointing defenders of the church, so as to drive them from their basilicas. You who rebuke me, why do you not first amend yourself?
Fulgentius said: We took the basilicas from our schismatics in order to restore them to the true Church.

Augustine answered: Our people did the same to you: they took [them] from their schismatics and handed them over to the Catholic mother. What your people did for the peace of Donatus, ours did for the peace of the body of Christ.
Fulgentius said: You are the schismatics, who both offered incense and handed over the books.

Augustine answered: Let us become weak with the weak, so that we may win the weak. I see what cannot be: the party of Donatus has conquered the whole of Christ, a corner of Africa has shut out the world, one nation has condemned all nations, the cutting has cut off the vine and the little twigs have lopped off the trees. At least you should keep what your predecessors laid down concerning us: you should not rebaptise, but set free through penance souls that, as you think, are straying. Reread the decrees of your fathers and see what they decreed ought to be done about traditors, those who offered incense, and schismatics, when they had come to Carthage in conspiracy against Caecilian. Your Marcianus, among others, gave the following judgement, which the seventy who were present certainly approve, since they do not disapprove it: 'In his Gospel,' he says, 'the Lord says: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. Every branch in me that does not bear fruit he will cut off and throw away, and every one that abides in me and bears fruit he prunes. As therefore unfruitful branches are cut off and thrown away, so those who offered incense, traditors, those abhorrent to God, cannot remain in the Church of God, unless, their wailing being recognised, they are reconciled through penance. Hence one ought not to communicate with Caecilian, ordained in schism by traditors.'

This is the settled judgement of your fathers. Look: suppose, God forbid, that we handed over [the books], that we offered incense, that we committed schism: why do you transgress the commandment of the elders in order to establish your own traditions? As unfruitful branches, he says, are cut off and thrown away, so those who offered incense, traditors, and those who are ordained in schism by traditors cannot remain in the Church of God, unless, their wailing being recognised, they are reconciled through penance: through penance, not through dipping. If you will deign [to listen], let at least your own leaders overcome you. Either confirm their decrees and lay aside your own inventions, or, if you want your own statutes to stand, declare that they are in error. If truth reigns among you, why is your tradition at odds [with itself]? The Saviour in his Gospel says this: Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste. And therefore, since your kingdom is divided in religion, destruction must follow upon the division. Amen.
